tool.name: Download and build MetaPhlAn database
tool.help:
What it does ============
This tool runs ``metaphlan --install --index <index> --bowtie2db <dir>`` for one selected database: it downloads the prebuilt Bowtie2 indexes plus ``<index>.pkl``, the ``_SGB``/``_VSG`` sequence files and ``_VINFO.csv`` from ``cmprod1.cibio.unitn.it/biobakery4/metaphlan_databases`` (md5 verified), extracts them below the chosen directory and adds one row to the ``metaphlan_database_versioned`` data table, from which the MetaPhlAn and HUMAnN tools choose their database. The job needs outbound HTTP(S) access to that host and roughly the download size as free disk.
Available databases ===================
- ``mpa_vJan21_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202103`` - release vJan21, 2.6 GB, for HUMAnN 3.5 to 3.6.1 - ``mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202212`` - release vOct22, 2.9 GB, for HUMAnN 3.7 and 3.8 - ``mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403`` - release vOct22, 2.7 GB, likewise (rebuilt) - ``mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202307`` - release vJun23, 3.2 GB, for HUMAnN 3.9 - ``mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403`` - release vJun23, 3.2 GB, likewise (rebuilt) - ``mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503`` - release vJan25, 4.9 GB, MetaPhlAn 4.2 and later only - ``mpa_vJan21_TOY_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202103`` - 1 MB, for demos and tests
MetaPhlAn itself can profile with any SGB database; HUMAnN is the picky consumer. It does not accept a version range but one or two specific marker releases, because it checks the profile header (e.g. for ``vJun23``) and because it needs an SGB-to-pangenome map that is generated per marker release. ``vJan25`` and later are rejected by every released HUMAnN.
Prefer the ``_202403`` builds: the ``_202212``/``_202307`` originals truncate profile lines (upstream ships a fixing script; the ``_202403`` rebuilds already contain the fix).
Naming scheme =============
The name packs two independent pieces of information, e.g. ``mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202212``:
- ``vOct22`` is the **marker release tag**. It changes when the SGB marker set changes (``vJan21`` -> ``vOct22`` -> ``vJun23`` -> ``vJan25``) and it is what downstream tools test against the profile header - this is the part to select for. - ``_202212`` is the **build date of that tarball**, not a version. A release is rebuilt when bugs are fixed (``_202212`` -> ``_202403``), which is why the same build date suffix exists under more than one release tag.
``mpa_v30_CHOCOPhlAn_201901`` (MetaPhlAn 3.0, 366 MB) has no release tag and a different file format. It is not offered here: MetaPhlAn 4.x looks for it under a path where it no longer exists, so it has to be fetched from the ``biobakery3`` directory by hand and added to the table with ``db_version = legacy``. The Galaxy tools then pass ``--mpa3`` when they see that value.
Table columns =============
- ``value`` - ``<index>-<DDMMYYYY>``. It carries the install date, so re-running this tool for the same index adds a second row instead of replacing the first: delete the old row before installing again. Rows added by hand should omit the date (a workflow step that pins ``value`` would otherwise not be portable between servers). - ``name`` - free text, shown in the tool forms. - ``dbkey`` - the database index, i.e. the value passed to ``metaphlan --index``. - ``path`` - the directory holding the database. - ``db_version`` - ``SGB`` for every database offered here, ``legacy`` for a pre-v4 one.
There is deliberately no "latest" choice: upstream's ``mpa_latest`` currently points at ``mpa_vJan26_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202611``, which no released HUMAnN can use.
Companion software ==================
HUMAnN 3.x needs MetaPhlAn 4.1.1 or older in its own environment: 4.2 renamed the command line options of the prescreen step, and 4.1.2 changed the output of ``metaphlan --version``, which HUMAnN parses (the run then stops with "CRITICAL ERROR: Can not call software version for metaphlan"). This concerns the *tool* version, not the database, which is plain data.
